Provides a Python web microframework that routes HTTP requests to view functions, normalizes diverse return types into Response objects, serves static files safely, and renders templates with Jinja.

Supports modular app structure with Blueprints: namespaced routes, URL prefixes, static/template assets, per-blueprint before/after/teardown hooks, URL defaults/value preprocessors, and blueprint-specific error handlers.

Manages application and request contexts with context-local proxies (current_app, request, session, g), deterministic push/pop and teardown callbacks, and lifecycle signals for requests and template rendering.

Offers flexible configuration management: dict-like config loaded from files, modules, environment variables (with prefixes and nested keys), instance folders, and attribute accessors with optional type conversion.
Provides a powerful CLI that discovers apps or factories automatically, loads .env, honors debug flags, exposes app and blueprint command groups, and runs commands within an application context.

Implements robust error handling and HTTP method behavior: register handlers by exception or status, wrap unexpected errors as 500, support abort(), and auto-generate OPTIONS/HEAD with 405/404 handling.

Delivers JSON utilities with a pluggable provider for dumps/loads/jsonify, HTML-safe serialization, file I/O, and a tagged serializer to round-trip nonstandard Python types (used for sessions and custom data).
Supplies secure, signed cookie-based sessions with configurable lifetimes and attributes, lazy write semantics, invalid/expired cookie handling, and JSON-tagged serialization for complex data.

Enforces request safety and limits: per-request and global content length, form memory/part limits, JSON parsing conditioned on content type with silent/force options, trusted host validation, and safe file-serving with conditional requests and cache controls.
Integrates logging tailored to Flask apps: app-named loggers, default streaming to WSGI errors or stderr, debug-aware log levels, and helpers to avoid duplicate handlers or unintended propagation.

Supports synchronous and asynchronous endpoints, class-based views (View/MethodView), method-specific decorators, automatic HEAD/OPTIONS inclusion, and typed contracts for lifecycle hooks and return values.

Provides comprehensive testing utilities: a test client with JSON support and redirect following, environment builders that use app config to construct correct URLs, session transactions, and reliable app/request context managers.

Includes examples and documentation: a tutorial blog with auth and SQLite/CLI, JavaScript/AJAX endpoints, a Celery integration demonstrating background tasks and progress APIs, and Sphinx-based docs with cross-references and project links.
